### Rules the payload model enforces

- **StatmechUploadRequest.normalize_text_fields** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `point_group`, `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_electronic_levels** (model, after; can refuse): electronic_levels level_index values must be unique.
- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_unique_calculation_keys** (model, after; can refuse): Statmech calculations must have unique keys.
- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model, after; can refuse via `raise_for_blocking_findings`):

  Refuse inline frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008). The inline
  calculations are scoped to this upload's species entry, so the
  declared kind and the parsed ``n_imag`` are both present here.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_source_calculation_keys_exist** (model, after; can refuse):

  Every *local* citation must name a calculation this request declares.

  Chained citations (``existing_calculation_id``) carry no key and
  are skipped here on purpose: the row they name was deposited by an
  earlier request, so this payload cannot possibly declare it. They
  are not thereby unchecked — existence, owner-consistency and
  role/type compatibility are all enforced against the database in
  :func:`app.services.statmech_resolution.resolve_or_create_statmech`,
  which is the only place that can check them.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model, after; can refuse):

  Refuse a repeated link, whichever way the calculation is named.

  ``statmech_source_calculation`` is keyed on ``(statmech_id,
  calculation_id, role)``, so a duplicate is a primary-key violation
  surfacing as a 500. The reference is now two-valued, so the
  uniqueness tuple carries both halves — the same shape thermo's
  ``ThermoSourceCalculationIn`` uniqueness check uses.

  One duplicate this cannot see: the same calculation cited once by
  inline key and once by id. That is impossible in practice, because
  an inline calculation is minted by this request and so has no id an
  earlier request could have handed out; the database's own primary
  key remains the backstop either way.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_unique_torsion_indices** (model, after; can refuse): Torsion indices must be unique within a statmech upload.
- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_scientific_interpretation** (model, after; can refuse):

  Scope each requirement to the claim this record actually makes.

  ``statmech_treatment`` is deliberately NOT required. Real producers
  (ARC among them) deposit symmetry, rotational constants and a
  frequency scale factor without naming a treatment; an absent field is
  honest where an invented one would not be.

  Source calculations are likewise not required here. A monatomic
  species has no vibrational modes to point at, and an experimental,
  literature or imported statmech has no calculation at all — forcing
  either to fabricate one buys nothing. Their absence on a *computed*
  record is reported as a structured upload warning at the workflow
  seam, and is enforced as an error only where a rate coefficient
  actually depends on it (the kinetics interpretation seam).

  What IS enforced is the one claim that is self-contradictory when
  unsupported: a rotor-aware treatment is *defined* by the internal
  rotors it treats, so it must list them. With no torsions the correct
  treatment is plain ``rrho``.

- **StatmechUploadRequest.validate_torsion_scan_calculation_keys** (model, after; can refuse): torsions[{i}].source_scan_calculation_key '{key}' does not reference a declared calculation.

## Surface `ThermoUploadRequest`

Workflow-facing thermo upload payload.

Payload model `app.schemas.workflows.thermo_upload.ThermoUploadRequest`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/ThermoUploadRequest.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`enthalpy_declaration_absent`](#c-enthalpy-declaration-absent) (422): Enthalpy content requires enthalpy_reference_kind.
- [`enthalpy_declaration_without_content`](#c-enthalpy-declaration-without-content) (422): enthalpy_reference_kind declares a quantity this thermo record does not carry.
- [`enthalpy_quantity_not_storable_here`](#c-enthalpy-quantity-not-storable-here) (422): Thermo accepts only formation_298k enthalpies.
- [`enthalpy_reference_kind_unrecognized`](#c-enthalpy-reference-kind-unrecognized) (422): '{reference}' is not a recognized enthalpy_reference_kind -- did you mean '{canonical}'?
- [`calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-calculation-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Every geometry linked to a calculation is made of the atoms of the subject that calculation is filed under -- the species entry's own formula, or, for a transition state, the sum of its reaction's reactants.
- [`species_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Species geometry is {geometry_formula}, but species_entry.smiles={payload.smiles} is {identity_formula} (species_geometry_composition_mismatch).
- [`species_geometry_isotope_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-isotope-mismatch) (422): Isotope substitution declared in species_entry.smiles does not match the uploaded geometry. smiles={_render(from_smiles)}; geometry.isotopes={_render(from_geometry)}.
- [`species_kind_conflict`](#c-species-kind-conflict) (422): This deposit declares molecule_kind={payload.molecule_kind.value}, but the species identity it resolves to (smiles={species.smiles}, charge={species.charge}, multiplicity={species.multiplicity}) is already stored as molecule_kind={species.kind.value} (species_kind_conflict).

### Rules the payload model enforces

- **ThermoUploadRequest.normalize_text_fields** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **ThermoUploadRequest.apply_computed_origin_defaults** (model, after):

  Fill the ``phase`` default only for computed uploads.

  A computed QC record's thermo values come from an ideal-gas
  rigid-rotor/harmonic-oscillator treatment, so ``phase`` defaults to
  ``gas`` when the uploader omits it. For experimental/literature/
  estimated origins the field stays ``None`` unless explicitly
  provided — defaulting it would silently stamp e.g. a
  condensed-phase literature value as ``gas``.

  ``reference_pressure_bar`` is NEVER defaulted, for any origin
  (decided 2026-09-24, issue #529): an omitted pressure is stored as not
  stated, never assumed to be 1 bar or 1 atm.

  Explicit values (including an explicit ``None``) are honored:
  ``model_fields_set`` distinguishes "omitted" from "provided".

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_temperature_range** (model, after; can refuse): tmin_k must be less than or equal to tmax_k.
- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_unique_points** (model, after; can refuse): Thermo points must be unique by temperature_k.
- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_unique_calculation_keys** (model, after; can refuse): Thermo calculations must have unique keys.
- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model, after; can refuse via `raise_for_blocking_findings`):

  Refuse inline frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008). The inline
  calculations are scoped to this upload's species entry, so the
  declared kind and the parsed ``n_imag`` are both present here.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_source_calculation_keys_exist** (model, after; can refuse):

  Every source_calculations[*].calculation_key, when provided, must
  reference a calculation declared in this upload. Entries that use
  ``existing_calculation_id`` instead are skipped — those are resolved
  against the database in the workflow layer.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model, after; can refuse): source_calculations must be unique by (calculation_key, existing_calculation_id, role).
- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_applied_correction_source_calc_keys** (model, after; can refuse):

  Every applied_energy_corrections[*].source_calculation_key, when
  provided, must reference a calculation declared in this upload. This
  prevents silent provenance loss where a correction would otherwise
  persist with a NULL source_calculation_id.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_energy_level_requires_no_statmech_link** (model, after; can refuse):

  ``energy_level_of_theory`` is meaningless once a statmech basis
  is linked: the record's levels then come entirely from that
  statmech record (R6), and there is no local 'opt'/'sp' link left
  for this field to be checked against. Refuse the combination
  outright rather than silently ignoring one of the two — the
  depositor almost certainly meant one or the other.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_group_additivity_origin** (model, after; can refuse):

  A GA breakdown may only attach to an ``estimated`` thermo record.

  Group additivity *is* the estimation method; attaching it to a
  computed / experimental / literature record would misrepresent the
  record's scientific origin.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_has_scientific_content** (model, after; can refuse):

  Reject uploads that carry only identity/provenance and no thermo data.

  At least one of: a scalar thermo value (``h298_kj_mol`` or
  ``s298_j_mol_k`` or ``enthalpy_formation_0k_kj_mol``), a NASA-7 polynomial block, a NASA-9 interval set,
  a Wilhoit block, or one or more tabulated thermo points must be
  present. Provenance-only fields such as ``literature``,
  ``software_release``, ``workflow_tool_release``, and ``note`` do not
  count.

- **ThermoUploadRequest.validate_representation_consistency** (model, after; can refuse):

  Enforce a single temperature-dependent *fit* representation.

  At most one fit form {nasa (NASA-7), nasa9_intervals, wilhoit} may be
  populated — mixing e.g. a NASA-9 fit and a Wilhoit fit on one thermo
  record is ambiguous. Tabulated ``points`` are NOT a fit: they may
  accompany a fit as auxiliary evidence, or stand alone (tabulated).
  When ``model_kind`` is supplied it must match the primary
  representation (nasa7↔nasa, nasa9↔nasa9_intervals, wilhoit↔wilhoit,
  tabulated↔points-only, scalar↔none). When ``model_kind`` is None the
  backend infers it (a fit wins over points). NASA-9 interval indices
  must be unique and contiguous from 1.

### Rules the workflow applies

Found by tracing each route's handler through its direct calls: every function reached that is marked `@producer_rule` (printed in full) or declared in the scientific check register.

- [`canonical_species_identity`](#k-app-chemistry-species-canonical-species-identity) (block; `species_smiles_charge_mismatch`)
- [`assert_calculation_geometry_composition`](#k-app-services-calculation-geometry-composition-assert-calculation-geometry-composition) (block; `calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`)
- [`evaluate_frequency_list_linearity`](#k-app-services-frequency-geometry-linearity-evaluate-frequency-list-linearity) (warn; `freq_list_linear_mode_count_for_bent_geometry`, `freq_list_bent_mode_count_for_linear_geometry`)
- [`assert_declared_kind_matches_stored`](#k-app-services-species-resolution-assert-declared-kind-matches-stored) (block; `species_kind_conflict`)
- [`assert_geometry_composition_matches_identity`](#k-app-services-species-resolution-assert-geometry-composition-matches-identity) (block; `species_geometry_composition_mismatch`)
- [`assert_geometry_isotopes_match_identity`](#k-app-services-species-resolution-assert-geometry-isotopes-match-identity) (block; `species_geometry_isotope_mismatch`)
- **`tckdb_schemas.enthalpy_reference:enthalpy_reference_error`** (reached from `POST /api/v1/uploads/thermo`):

  A thermo record with enthalpy content must declare what its enthalpies mean.

  ``enthalpy_reference_kind`` accepts one value, ``formation_298k``: every
  enthalpy on the record is a standard enthalpy of formation, pinned at
  298.15 K, with the species' own increment above 298.15 K added at other
  temperatures. It is never defaulted or inferred. Any other value is
  refused; a near-miss spelling of ``formation_298k`` gets its own refusal.

  Enthalpy content, any of which requires ``enthalpy_reference_kind`` and
  without all of which a declaration is refused:

  * ``h298_kj_mol``;
  * a ``nasa`` block or ``nasa9_intervals`` (their enthalpy constants);
  * ``wilhoit.h0_kj_mol``;
  * a point ``h_kj_mol``;
  * a point ``g_kj_mol``. A tabulated Gibbs energy is H(T) - T*S(T) on the
    record's enthalpy zero, so it carries H's reference exactly as a point
    H does, even on a point with no H of its own.

  A 0 K formation scalar has its own reference and is outside this rule.
  Never derive a missing scalar from a fit or infer a declaration.

  Returns a refusal ``(code, message)``, or ``None`` for a coherent
  declaration.

<a id="s-thermomluploadrequest"></a>

## Surface `ThermoMLUploadRequest`

One ThermoML XML document, uploaded directly (not from the NIST bulk archive — that path is the ``--archive``/``--doi`` CLI only).

Payload model `app.schemas.workflows.thermoml_upload.ThermoMLUploadRequest`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/ThermoMLUploadRequest.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`thermoml_doi_conflict`](#c-thermoml-doi-conflict) (422): the supplied doi {explicit} does not match the uploaded file's own sDOI {document}
- [`thermoml_file_too_large`](#c-thermoml-file-too-large) (422): ThermoML file exceeds the maximum upload size of {MAX_THERMOML_UPLOAD_BYTES} bytes.
- [`thermoml_invalid_base64`](#c-thermoml-invalid-base64) (422): content_base64 must contain only ASCII characters.
- [`thermoml_no_supported_content`](#c-thermoml-no-supported-content) (422): No mappable ideal-gas or real-gas Cp(T) content was found in this file.
- [`thermoml_schema_invalid`](#c-thermoml-schema-invalid) (422): see the code reference
- [`rights_attestation_not_depositor`](#c-rights-attestation-not-depositor) (403): only the account that made the deposit can attest a depositor agreement for it.
- [`rights_attestation_requires_curator`](#c-rights-attestation-requires-curator) (403): a {basis.value} attestation records a curator's judgement and needs the curator or admin role.
- [`rights_license_blank`](#c-rights-license-blank) (422): a rights attestation must name a license.

### Routes

| Method and path | Success | Idempotency-Key | Path parameters | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/uploads/thermoml` | 201 | required | none | `app.api.routes.uploads.upload_thermoml` |

`POST /api/v1/uploads/thermoml` says:

> Accept one ThermoML XML document directly -- not from the NIST bulk
> archive that ``backend/scripts/thermoml_cp_import.py --archive``
> reads. Anyone authenticated may deposit one (Phase C-E6, "let anyone
> ingest a ThermoML file, not only the NIST archive").
>
> Transport mirrors ``ArtifactIn.content_base64`` (the only other
> inline-file-bytes schema in this codebase): JSON body,
> base64-encoded content, decoded and size-checked here before the
> pipeline runs at all -- the encoded-length pre-check
> (``MAX_ENCODED_ARTIFACT_LEN``) rejects an oversized payload before
> the decode allocation, the decoded-length check catches base64
> padding slack.
>
> Idempotency: unlike every sibling ``/uploads/*`` route (where the
> ``Idempotency-Key`` header is optional -- DR-0024 does not make it
> mandatory in general), this specific route requires it, by the C-E6
> decision (2026-09-20; "C-E6 -- ThermoML file input and upload route",
> ``docs/research/tckdb-phase-c-implementation-plan.md``). A request
> without the header never reaches this function's body at all:
> FastAPI's own required-header validation (see the
> ``_idempotency_key_required`` parameter above) answers with its
> ordinary 422 first.
>
> Rights: ``request.rights`` (``DepositRights``) is required on this
> schema -- unlike every sibling upload schema, where it is optional
> and absence "bites at release time, not at upload". This route's
> whole content is a third-party document the depositor is asserting
> the right to submit, with no fallback source terms to stand on
> instead (see ``ThermoMLUploadRequest.rights`` for the full
> reasoning), so omitting it is refused by ordinary Pydantic
> field-requiredness before this function's body runs.
>
> No preview: unlike the CLI (``--commit`` default-off), this route
> always commits, like every sibling ``/uploads/*`` route -- none of
> them preview a request before writing it (see
> ``ThermoMLUploadRequest``'s docstring for the one preview mechanism
> that does exist in this codebase, and why it does not apply here).

### Payload fields

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Unit | Values / constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `filename` | string | yes |  |  | length >= 1; length <= 255 | Provenance metadata only — recorded verbatim (as ``f"upload:{filename}"``) in the custody row's ``mapping_report_json["source_label"]``. Never used as a storage path (the object store is content-addressed by SHA-256) and never used as a fallback ``raw_uri`` the way an archive member path is (see ``app.services.thermoml_cp_import._raw_uri_for``'s ``allow_member_path_fallback``) — it is a display label, not a retrievable location. |
| `content_base64` | string | yes |  |  | length >= 1 | Base64-encoded ThermoML XML bytes. |
| `doi` | string \| null | no | `null` |  | length <= 255 | The article's own DOI, if the depositor wants to assert it explicitly. Optional — when omitted, the DOI is taken from the file's own ``Citation/sDOI`` element, if present. Supplying one that disagrees with the file's own ``sDOI`` is a refusal (``thermoml_doi_conflict``), never a silent override. |
| `rights` | [`DepositRights`](#m-depositrights) | yes |  |  |  | The depositor's deposit-time license agreement. Required — deliberately **not** optional like ``DepositRights`` on every other upload schema. Every other upload route can fall back on "attested later, at release time" because the underlying science already exists in TCKDB under someone's authority; this route's whole content *is* a third-party document the depositor is asserting the right to submit, and unlike the CLI's ``--archive`` path there is no NIST/TRC ``source_terms`` to stand on instead. Omitting it is refused by ordinary Pydantic field-requiredness (422, the same mechanism every other required field on every other schema in this codebase already uses — not a new bespoke refusal). Recorded as an ordinary ``depositor_agreement`` attestation, never ``source_terms``. |

Nested models (1; fields and rules in the [model reference](#model-reference)):

- [`DepositRights`](#m-depositrights)

## Surface `TransitionStateUploadRequest`

Workflow-facing transition-state upload payload.

Payload model `tckdb_schemas.workflows.transition_state_upload.TransitionStateUploadRequest`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/TransitionStateUploadRequest.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`atom_map_contradicts_irc_mapping`](#c-atom-map-contradicts-irc-mapping) (422): Transition state '{subject_label}' {field_path} contradicts its own IRC participant mapping: the atom map assigns saddle-point atom(s) {disputed} to {offender[0].value} {offender[1]}, which the IRC mapping assigns to {', '.join(elsewhere) or 'no participant'} ({W_ATOM_MAP_CONTRADICTS_IRC_MAPPING}).
- [`atom_map_inferred_requires_note`](#c-atom-map-inferred-requires-note) (422): atom_map.source='inferred' requires atom_map.note naming the algorithm that produced the map.
- [`transition_state_charge_mismatch`](#c-transition-state-charge-mismatch) (422): Transition state '{subject_label}' carries charge {transition_state_charge}, but its reactants total {reactant_charge} (transition_state_charge_mismatch).
- [`transition_state_irc_mapping_element_mismatch`](#c-transition-state-irc-mapping-element-mismatch) (422): Transition state '{subject_label}' {field_path} assigns saddle-point atoms {sorted(atom_indices)} to {participant_key}, which is {format_element_counts(assigned)}, but {role.value} {participant_index} is declared as '{species.smiles}', which is {format_element_counts(declared)} ({W_IRC_MAPPING_ELEMENT_MISMATCH}).
- [`reaction_charge_not_conserved`](#c-reaction-charge-not-conserved) (422): Reaction reactants total charge {reactant_charge} but products total {product_charge} (reaction_charge_not_conserved).
- [`reaction_mass_balance_failed`](#c-reaction-mass-balance-failed) (422): Reaction is not element-balanced (reaction_mass_balance_failed).
- [`calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-calculation-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Every geometry linked to a calculation is made of the atoms of the subject that calculation is filed under -- the species entry's own formula, or, for a transition state, the sum of its reaction's reactants.
- [`n_imag_contradicts_minimum`](#c-n-imag-contradicts-minimum) (422): A species entry declared a minimum has no imaginary vibrational modes.

### Routes

| `POST /api/v1/jobs/transition-state` | 202 | optional | none | `app.api.routes.jobs.enqueue_transition_state` |

Optional but strongly recommended: a deposit without it succeeds and returns a 'transition_state_missing_irc_evidence' upload warning. ### Rules the payload model enforces

- **TransitionStateUploadRequest.normalize_text** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `label`, `note`, `unmapped_smiles`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **TransitionStateUploadRequest.validate_primary_opt_is_opt** (model, after; can refuse): primary_opt must have type 'opt', got '{self.primary_opt.type.value}'.
- **TransitionStateUploadRequest.validate_validation_evidence** (model, after; can refuse):

  Bind IRC evidence to this upload's single ``irc`` calculation.

  There are no bundle-local calculation keys here, so the locator is the
  calculation itself: evidence is only depositable alongside exactly one
  ``irc`` additional calculation. That is not a limitation invented
  here — ``transition_state_validation_evidence`` stores a single
  ``reconstruction_calculation_id``, so one evidence record can only ever
  name one calculation.

- **TransitionStateUploadRequest.validate_additional_calculation_types** (model, after; can refuse): Additional calculation type '{calc.type.value}' is not allowed. Expected one of: {', '.join((t.value for t in sorted(_ALLOWED_ADDITIONAL_TYPES, key=lambda t: t.value)))}.
- **TransitionStateUploadRequest.validate_reaction_coordinate_contract** (model, after; can refuse via `raise_for_blocking_findings`):

  Refuse frequency evidence with no usable reaction coordinate.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008, narrowed by ADR
  0012: at least one imaginary mode, exactly one designated the
  reaction coordinate, and no undeclared mode stiff enough to make
  that designation meaningless).

## Surface `TransportUploadRequest`

Workflow-facing standalone transport upload payload.

Payload model `app.schemas.workflows.transport_upload.TransportUploadRequest`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/TransportUploadRequest.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-calculation-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Every geometry linked to a calculation is made of the atoms of the subject that calculation is filed under -- the species entry's own formula, or, for a transition state, the sum of its reaction's reactants.
- [`species_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Species geometry is {geometry_formula}, but species_entry.smiles={payload.smiles} is {identity_formula} (species_geometry_composition_mismatch).
- [`species_geometry_isotope_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-isotope-mismatch) (422): Isotope substitution declared in species_entry.smiles does not match the uploaded geometry. smiles={_render(from_smiles)}; geometry.isotopes={_render(from_geometry)}.
- [`species_kind_conflict`](#c-species-kind-conflict) (422): This deposit declares molecule_kind={payload.molecule_kind.value}, but the species identity it resolves to (smiles={species.smiles}, charge={species.charge}, multiplicity={species.multiplicity}) is already stored as molecule_kind={species.kind.value} (species_kind_conflict).
- [`species_smiles_charge_mismatch`](#c-species-smiles-charge-mismatch) (422): species_entry.charge={payload.charge} does not match SMILES charge {charge}
- [`calculation_key_undeclared`](#c-calculation-key-undeclared) (422): Transition state '{ts.key}' validation evidence references undefined calculation_key '{evidence.source_calculation_key}'.
- [`calculation_software_is_workflow_tool`](#c-calculation-software-is-workflow-tool) (422): software_release.name={software_release.name} names {tool}, a workflow tool, not the electronic-structure program that ran this calculation.
- [`freq_mode_index_not_unique`](#c-freq-mode-index-not-unique) (422): mode_index values must be unique within a freq result.

### Routes

| Method and path | Success | Idempotency-Key | Path parameters | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/uploads/transport` | 201 | optional | none | `app.api.routes.uploads.upload_transport` |
| `POST /api/v1/jobs/transport` | 202 | optional | none | `app.api.routes.jobs.enqueue_transport` |

`POST /api/v1/uploads/transport` says:

> Create a standalone transport record for a resolvable species entry.
>
> The request carries the target species-entry identity, transport
> properties, provenance references, and optional inline supporting
> calculations with role links. Transport is append-only — repeated
> uploads against the same species entry create independent rows.

### Rules the payload model enforces

- **TransportUploadRequest.normalize_text** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **TransportUploadRequest.validate_has_scientific_content** (model, after; can refuse):

  Reject uploads that carry only identity/provenance and no transport data.

  At least one of ``sigma_angstrom``, ``epsilon_over_k_k``,
  ``dipole_debye``, ``polarizability_angstrom3``, or
  ``rotational_relaxation`` must be present. Provenance-only fields such
  as ``literature``, ``software_release``, ``workflow_tool_release``, and
  ``note`` do not count.

  A transport row carrying none of these is definitionally empty — it
  claims to be transport data while carrying no transport property — so
  this is a contract violation and blocks at upload, per ADR 0008
  (``docs/adr/0008-validation-tiers-definitions-block-expectations-warn.md``).
  The read-time counterpart is the backend's
  ``HardFailReason.no_transport_property_present``, which this check owns
  as the blocking tier; the trust label remains as a backstop for rows
  that entered by a non-upload path.

- **TransportUploadRequest.validate_lj_pair** (model, after; can refuse): Require Lennard-Jones sigma and epsilon/k to be provided together.
- **TransportUploadRequest.validate_unique_calculation_keys** (model, after; can refuse): Transport calculations must have unique keys.
- **TransportUploadRequest.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model, after; can refuse via `raise_for_blocking_findings`):

  Refuse inline frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008). The inline
  calculations are scoped to this upload's species entry, so the
  declared kind and the parsed ``n_imag`` are both present here.

- **TransportUploadRequest.validate_source_calculation_keys_exist** (model, after; can refuse):

  Every ``source_calculations[*].calculation_key`` must reference a
  calculation declared in this upload.

- **TransportUploadRequest.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model, after; can refuse): source_calculations must be unique by (calculation_key, role).

## Surface `ContributionBundleV0`

Top-level contribution bundle v0 envelope.

Payload model `app.schemas.workflows.contribution_bundle.ContributionBundleV0`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/ContributionBundleV0.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`enthalpy_declaration_absent`](#c-enthalpy-declaration-absent) (422): Enthalpy content requires enthalpy_reference_kind.
- [`enthalpy_declaration_without_content`](#c-enthalpy-declaration-without-content) (422): enthalpy_reference_kind declares a quantity this thermo record does not carry.
- [`enthalpy_quantity_not_storable_here`](#c-enthalpy-quantity-not-storable-here) (422): Thermo accepts only formation_298k enthalpies.
- [`enthalpy_reference_kind_unrecognized`](#c-enthalpy-reference-kind-unrecognized) (422): '{reference}' is not a recognized enthalpy_reference_kind -- did you mean '{canonical}'?
- [`reaction_charge_not_conserved`](#c-reaction-charge-not-conserved) (422): Reaction reactants total charge {reactant_charge} but products total {product_charge} (reaction_charge_not_conserved).
- [`reaction_mass_balance_failed`](#c-reaction-mass-balance-failed) (422): Reaction is not element-balanced (reaction_mass_balance_failed).
- [`calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-calculation-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Every geometry linked to a calculation is made of the atoms of the subject that calculation is filed under -- the species entry's own formula, or, for a transition state, the sum of its reaction's reactants.
- [`species_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-species-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Species geometry is {geometry_formula}, but species_entry.smiles={payload.smiles} is {identity_formula} (species_geometry_composition_mismatch).

### Routes

| Method and path | Success | Idempotency-Key | Path parameters | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/bundles/dry-run` | 200 | not accepted | none | `app.api.routes.bundles.dry_run_bundle` |
| `POST /api/v1/bundles/submit` | 201 | optional | none | `app.api.routes.bundles.submit_bundle` |

`POST /api/v1/bundles/dry-run` says:

> Preview what a real import would do, and whether submit would accept it.
>
> Requires authentication (session cookie or API key). Returns a
> structured preview describing which identities would be reused,
> which would be created, and that thermo/kinetics result rows would
> be appended.
>
> Then rehearses ``/bundles/submit`` for the same bundle — the same
> function, inside a savepoint that is always rolled back — so every
> check submit applies is applied here too. If submit would refuse the
> bundle, the result carries that refusal as an ``error`` message with
> submit's own ``code`` and message, and ``bundle_valid`` is false.
> Nothing is kept: the rehearsal's writes are rolled back and this
> session never commits.
>
> If another deposit holds a lock the rehearsal needs, the rehearsal gives
> way rather than delay or deadlock that deposit, and this route answers
> ``503 dry_run_contended`` with a ``Retry-After`` header: nothing was
> decided about the bundle, and retrying is the right response.
>
> A bundle over the size caps -- ``413 bundle_too_large`` for the request
> body, ``422 bundle_too_many_records`` for the record count -- is refused
> before any rehearsal, exactly as ``/bundles/submit`` refuses it. This
> route has its own, tighter rate bucket.

`POST /api/v1/bundles/submit` says:

> Import a contribution bundle into the hosted database.
>
> Requires authentication (session cookie or API key). Runs the dry-run
> preview as a strict gate (any error or unsupported action blocks the
> import), then imports thermo or kinetics records through the existing
> upload workflows, creates a ``submission`` plus matching audit/link
> rows, and returns a structured result.
>
> Imported rows are publicly visible by default but explicitly
> ``unreviewed``: validation means importable, not curated/approved.
> Transaction management lives in ``get_write_db`` — any failure rolls
> back the whole bundle (no partial imports). Sending an
> ``Idempotency-Key`` header makes the submit retry-safe; an exact retry
> replays the stored response without re-importing the bundle.
>
> A bundle over the size caps is refused as ``/bundles/dry-run`` refuses
> it: ``413 bundle_too_large`` (request body) or
> ``422 bundle_too_many_records``.

### Rules the payload model enforces

- **ContributionBundleV0.validate_records_match_kind** (model, after; can refuse):

  - thermo bundles must contain at least one thermo_uploads entry.
  - thermo bundles must not carry kinetics_uploads in v0; mixed bundles are not supported.
  - kinetics bundles must contain at least one kinetics_uploads entry.
  - kinetics bundles must not carry thermo_uploads in v0; mixed bundles are not supported.

- **ContributionBundleV0.validate_local_ref_keys** (model, after; can refuse):

  - local_refs key {key} is malformed; expected '<namespace>:<label>' (e.g. 'species:ethanol').
  - local_refs key {key} uses a purely numeric label; raw DB primary keys must not be used as local refs.

### Rules the workflow applies

Found by tracing each route's handler through its direct calls: every function reached that is marked `@producer_rule` (printed in full) or declared in the scientific check register.

- [`canonical_species_identity`](#k-app-chemistry-species-canonical-species-identity) (block; `species_smiles_charge_mismatch`)
- [`assert_calculation_geometry_composition`](#k-app-services-calculation-geometry-composition-assert-calculation-geometry-composition) (block; `calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`)
- [`validate_reaction_charge_conservation`](#k-app-services-reaction-resolution-validate-reaction-charge-conservation) (block; `reaction_charge_not_conserved`)
- [`validate_reaction_elemental_balance`](#k-app-services-reaction-resolution-validate-reaction-elemental-balance) (block; `reaction_mass_balance_failed`)
- [`assert_declared_kind_matches_stored`](#k-app-services-species-resolution-assert-declared-kind-matches-stored) (block; `species_kind_conflict`)
- [`assert_geometry_composition_matches_identity`](#k-app-services-species-resolution-assert-geometry-composition-matches-identity) (block; `species_geometry_composition_mismatch`)
- [`assert_geometry_isotopes_match_identity`](#k-app-services-species-resolution-assert-geometry-isotopes-match-identity) (block; `species_geometry_isotope_mismatch`)
- **`tckdb_schemas.enthalpy_reference:enthalpy_reference_error`** (reached from `POST /api/v1/bundles/dry-run`, `POST /api/v1/bundles/submit`):

  A thermo record with enthalpy content must declare what its enthalpies mean.

  ``enthalpy_reference_kind`` accepts one value, ``formation_298k``: every
  enthalpy on the record is a standard enthalpy of formation, pinned at
  298.15 K, with the species' own increment above 298.15 K added at other
  temperatures. It is never defaulted or inferred. Any other value is
  refused; a near-miss spelling of ``formation_298k`` gets its own refusal.

  Enthalpy content, any of which requires ``enthalpy_reference_kind`` and
  without all of which a declaration is refused:

  * ``h298_kj_mol``;
  * a ``nasa`` block or ``nasa9_intervals`` (their enthalpy constants);
  * ``wilhoit.h0_kj_mol``;
  * a point ``h_kj_mol``;
  * a point ``g_kj_mol``. A tabulated Gibbs energy is H(T) - T*S(T) on the
    record's enthalpy zero, so it carries H's reference exactly as a point
    H does, even on a point with no H of its own.

  A 0 K formation scalar has its own reference and is outside this rule.
  Never derive a missing scalar from a fit or infer a declaration.

  Returns a refusal ``(code, message)``, or ``None`` for a coherent
  declaration.

## Surface `ArtifactsUploadRequest`

Inline batch artifact upload payload.

Payload model `app.api.routes.calculations.ArtifactsUploadRequest`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/ArtifactsUploadRequest.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`calculation_geometry_composition_mismatch`](#c-calculation-geometry-composition-mismatch) (422): Every geometry linked to a calculation is made of the atoms of the subject that calculation is filed under -- the species entry's own formula, or, for a transition state, the sum of its reaction's reactants.
- [`handle_not_found`](#c-handle-not-found) (404): see the code reference
- [`handle_type_mismatch`](#c-handle-type-mismatch) (422): expected a {kind_label} {noun} (prefix {expected_prefix}) but got prefix {prefix}
- [`invalid_handle`](#c-invalid-handle) (422): {stripped} is neither an integer id nor a <prefix>_<body> public ref
- [`tckdb_client_version_invalid`](#c-tckdb-client-version-invalid) (426): see the code reference
- [`tckdb_client_version_missing`](#c-tckdb-client-version-missing) (426): see the code reference
- [`tckdb_client_version_unsupported`](#c-tckdb-client-version-unsupported) (426): see the code reference

### Routes

| Method and path | Success | Idempotency-Key | Path parameters | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/calculations/{calculation_id}/artifacts` | 201 | optional | `calculation_id` (string) | `app.api.routes.calculations.upload_calculation_artifacts` |

`POST /api/v1/calculations/{calculation_id}/artifacts` says:

> Attach one or more artifacts (logs, inputs, checkpoints) to a
> calculation.
>
> Second-phase upload: the calculation must already exist (typically
> created via ``POST /uploads/conformers`` or a contribution bundle).
> The upload is batch-atomic — any per-artifact validation failure in
> the request rejects the entire batch with 422 and no DB rows or S3
> writes are produced. If a storage write fails partway through pass-2,
> pending rows roll back and content-addressed objects are retained for
> reference-aware garbage collection; deleting a digest key eagerly could
> remove bytes shared with an existing record.
>
> A storage failure returns 503 (`artifact_storage_unavailable`) when the
> object store did not answer, and **507** (`artifact_storage_full`) when
> it answered and refused the write for want of room. The second is not
> transient from a depositor's side: an operator must free space or raise
> the store's quota, so retrying is futile until they do.
>
> Authorization (any one of):
>
> - the caller created the calculation (``calculation.created_by ==
>   current_user.id``);
> - the caller owns a live submission linked to this calculation
>   through ``submission_record_link`` (rejected/superseded
>   submissions do not qualify);
> - the caller has the ``curator`` or ``admin`` role.

### Payload fields

Unknown keys are silently ignored.

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Unit | Values / constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `artifacts` | array of [`ArtifactIn`](#m-artifactin) | yes |  |  | length >= 1 |  |

Nested models (1; fields and rules in the [model reference](#model-reference)):

- [`ArtifactIn`](#m-artifactin)

## Surface `RightsAttestationCreate`

Payload for recording who agreed to license a submission, and how.

Payload model `app.schemas.entities.submission.RightsAttestationCreate`; JSON Schema `tckdb_schemas/contract/schemas/RightsAttestationCreate.schema.json`.

### Will be refused if

The most specific refusals traced for this surface (ranking in the [code reference](#refusal-code-reference) intro):

- [`handle_not_found`](#c-handle-not-found) (404): see the code reference
- [`handle_type_mismatch`](#c-handle-type-mismatch) (422): expected a {kind_label} {noun} (prefix {expected_prefix}) but got prefix {prefix}
- [`invalid_handle`](#c-invalid-handle) (422): {stripped} is neither an integer id nor a <prefix>_<body> public ref
- [`rights_attestation_not_depositor`](#c-rights-attestation-not-depositor) (403): only the account that made the deposit can attest a depositor agreement for it.
- [`rights_attestation_requires_curator`](#c-rights-attestation-requires-curator) (403): a {basis.value} attestation records a curator's judgement and needs the curator or admin role.
- [`rights_license_blank`](#c-rights-license-blank) (422): a rights attestation must name a license.
- [`rights_source_terms_required`](#c-rights-source-terms-required) (422): a source_terms attestation must quote or cite the terms the records were taken under.
- [`tckdb_client_version_invalid`](#c-tckdb-client-version-invalid) (426): see the code reference

### Routes

| Method and path | Success | Idempotency-Key | Path parameters | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/submissions/{submission_id}/rights-attestations` | 201 | not accepted | `submission_id` (string) | `app.api.routes.submissions.create_rights_attestation` |

`POST /api/v1/submissions/{submission_id}/rights-attestations` says:

> Record who agrees to license this submission, and on what basis.
>
> A ``depositor_agreement`` is the depositor's own statement and is accepted
> only from the submission's creator; ``operator_own_data``,
> ``historical_review`` and ``source_terms`` record a curator's judgement
> and need the curator or admin role. Appending never edits: a new row
> supersedes the one that stood before.
>
> :raises HTTPException: 403 when the caller may not make this attestation;
>     422 for a body the caller can correct (blank license, missing
>     ``source_terms``).

| `source_terms` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |

`POST /api/v1/submissions/{submission_ref}/supersede` says:

> Mark a submission as superseded by another.
>
> Both submissions are named by public ref: the old one in the path, the
> replacing one in the body. A row id is refused by the ref pattern (422)
> in either place. The replacing submission must already declare the old
> one as the submission it supersedes -- supersession asserts the link, it
> does not create it. Returns the newly-superseded *old* submission.
>
> The caller must have created both submissions, or hold the curator or
> admin role -- the rule every read on this router applies, here applied
> to each of the two. Otherwise 403 ``submission_supersede_not_owner``.
> An unknown ref is 404 whoever asks.

Validated against `SubmissionSupersedeRequest` when this file was generated, but not accepted on its own: it needs two submissions of the caller's own: the one whose public ref is in the path, and a newer one created declaring that it supersedes it, whose public ref (public_ref on a submission read) replaces this one.

```json
{
  "new_submission_ref": "sub_01j9x8k3y2rm4f0x8k3y2rm4f0"
}
```

## Model reference

Every model a producer payload can contain, alphabetically. A payload's root model is specified in its surface section. Field descriptions come from the field's `description=` or the model's `:param name:` docstring entry; a blank description means the source has neither.

- **AppliedEnergyCorrectionInBundle.normalize_text_fields** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **AppliedEnergyCorrectionInBundle.validate_exactly_one_provenance_source** (model, after; can refuse): Exactly one of 'scheme' or 'frequency_scale_factor' must be provided.
- **AppliedEnergyCorrectionInBundle.validate_role_source_compatibility** (model, after; can refuse):

- **AppliedEnergyCorrectionInBundle.validate_role_scheme_kind_compatibility** (model, after; can refuse):

  Ensure the resolved scheme's ``kind`` is compatible with the
  applied correction's ``application_role``.

  This is the domain check above and beyond
  ``validate_role_source_compatibility`` — it doesn't only verify
  that *a* scheme was provided, but that the right *kind* of scheme
  was provided (e.g. ``aec_total`` must come from an
  ``atom_energy`` scheme, not a ``bac_petersson`` scheme).

  Roles absent from ``_ROLE_TO_REQUIRED_SCHEME_KINDS`` are
  unconstrained — they are escape hatches whose scheme.kind is
  producer-defined.

- **AppliedEnergyCorrectionInBundle.validate_fsf_requires_source_calculation** (model, after; can refuse): frequency_scale_factor requires source_calculation_key (the frequency calculation the scale factor was applied to).
- **AppliedEnergyCorrectionInBundle.validate_unique_components** (model, after; can refuse): Components must be unique by (component_kind, key).

<a id="m-bundlekineticsin"></a>

### `BundleKineticsIn`

`tckdb_schemas.workflows.computed_reaction_upload`.

One kinetics fit (Arrhenius parameters) within the bundle.

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Unit | Values / constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reactant_keys` | array of string | yes |  |  | length >= 1 | Species keys on the reactant side of this fit. |
| `product_keys` | array of string | yes |  |  | length >= 1 | Species keys on the product side of this fit. |
| `scientific_origin` | `ScientificOriginKind` | no | `"computed"` |  | `computed`, `experimental`, `estimated` | Scientific origin category. |
| `model_kind` | `KineticsModelKind` | no | `"modified_arrhenius"` |  | `arrhenius`, `modified_arrhenius`, `multi_arrhenius`, `lindemann`, `troe`, `sri`, `plog`, `chebyshev` | Kinetics functional form. |
| `is_third_body` | boolean | no | `false` |  |  | True for a simple ``+M`` third-body reaction (no falloff). |
| `a` | number \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Arrhenius pre-exponential factor. |
| `a_units` | `ArrheniusAUnits` \| null | no | `null` |  | `per_s`, `cm3_mol_s`, `cm3_molecule_s`, `m3_mol_s`, `cm6_mol2_s`, `cm6_molecule2_s`, `m6_mol2_s` | Units for A. |
| `n` | number \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Temperature exponent. |
| `reported_ea` | number \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Activation energy in reported units. |
| `reported_ea_units` | `ActivationEnergyUnits` \| null | no | `null` |  | `j_mol`, `kj_mol`, `cal_mol`, `kcal_mol` | Units for Ea. |
| `a_uncertainty` | number \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `a_uncertainty_kind` | `KineticsUncertaintyKind` \| null | no | `null` |  | `additive`, `multiplicative` |  |
| `n_uncertainty` | number \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `d_reported_ea` | number \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `tmin_k` | number \| null | no | `null` | K | > 0 | Minimum valid temperature. |
| `tmax_k` | number \| null | no | `null` | K | > 0 | Maximum valid temperature. |
| `degeneracy` | number \| null | no | `null` |  | > 0 | Optional finite, strictly positive multiplicative reaction-path degeneracy associated with the reported kinetics expression. ``None`` means no claim is made; do not interpret it as ``1.0``. |
| `degeneracy_convention` | `KineticsDegeneracyConvention` | no | `"unknown"` |  | `already_applied`, `not_applied`, `unknown` | Whether degeneracy is already included in the reported rate. Defaults to ``unknown`` for legacy producers. |
| `tunneling_model` | `TunnelingModel` \| null | no | `null` |  | `none`, `wigner`, `eckart`, `sct`, `other` | Optional tunneling model label. |
| `pressure_context` | `PressureContext` \| null | no | `null` |  | `high_p_limit`, `apparent_at_pressure`, `pressure_dependent` |  |
| `pressure_bar` | number \| null | no | `null` | bar | > 0 |  |
| `note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional note. |
| `source_calculations` | array of [`KineticsSourceCalculationIn`](#m-kineticssourcecalculationin) | no | `[]` |  |  | Producer-declared kinetics provenance: each entry references a calculation by bundle-local key with a scientific role. When non-empty, the workflow writes exactly these kinetics_source_calculation rows and skips the legacy auto-link fallback. When empty, the workflow falls back to auto-linking species-owned SP calculations as reactant_energy / product_energy (legacy convenience). |

- **BundleKineticsIn.normalize_text** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **BundleKineticsIn.validate_pressure_context** (model, after; can refuse): pressure_context='apparent_at_pressure' requires pressure_bar.
- **BundleKineticsIn.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model, after; can refuse): Duplicate kinetics source_calculations entry (calculation_key='{entry.calculation_key}', role='{entry.role.value}'). Each (calculation_key, role) pair must be declared at most once per kinetics fit.
- **BundleKineticsIn.validate_ea_pair** (model, after; can refuse): reported_ea and reported_ea_units must both be provided or both omitted.
- **BundleKineticsIn.validate_a_uncertainty_kind** (model, after; can refuse):

  - a_uncertainty and a_uncertainty_kind must both be provided or both omitted.
  - Multiplicative a_uncertainty must be >= 1.0 (factor f, with the true value within [A/f, A*f]).

- **BundleKineticsIn.validate_temperature_range** (model, after; can refuse): tmin_k must be <= tmax_k.
- **BundleKineticsIn.validate_model_kind_is_representable** (model, after; can refuse):

  Reject functional forms the bundle payload cannot carry.

  ``BundleKineticsIn`` only holds the *scalar* Arrhenius fields
  (``a``/``n``/``reported_ea``). The pressure-dependent and
  multi-term forms (``multi_arrhenius``, ``plog``, ``troe``,
  ``sri``, ``lindemann``, ``chebyshev``) each require child data
  (sum-of-Arrhenius terms, PLOG entries, falloff broadening,
  Chebyshev coefficients) for which this schema has no fields.
  Accepting them here would persist a self-contradictory
  ``kinetics`` row — tagged e.g. ``plog`` but carrying zero PLOG
  entries. Direct those uploads to the dedicated single-reaction
  kinetics endpoint, whose schema carries the child rows.

- **BundleKineticsIn._normalize_tunneling** (field, before on `tunneling_model`): applies `normalize_tunneling_model` to `tunneling_model`: Coerce a producer-supplied tunneling model to a canonical token.

<a id="m-bundlespeciesin"></a>

### `BundleSpeciesIn`

`tckdb_schemas.workflows.computed_reaction_upload`.

A species defined within this kinetics bundle.

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Unit | Values / constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |  |  | length >= 1 | Local key for referencing this species in the reaction. |
| `species_entry` | [`SpeciesEntryIdentityPayload`](#m-speciesentryidentitypayload) | yes |  |  |  | Species identity (SMILES, charge, multiplicity). |
| `conformers` | array of [`ConformerIn (computed_reaction_upload)`](#m-conformerin-computed-reaction-upload) | no | `[]` |  |  | Conformer observations (geometry + opt calculation). Each list item creates a distinct observation row, even when multiple items land in the same conformer group. |
| `calculations` | array of [`ComputedReactionCalculationIn`](#m-computedreactioncalculationin) | no | `[]` |  |  | Additional calculations (freq, sp at higher LOT). Their ``geometry_key``, when given, must reference one of this species's conformer geometries -- it names the geometry the calculation ran on. |
| `thermo` | [`BundleThermoIn`](#m-bundlethermoin) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional thermochemistry data. |
| `statmech` | [`BundleStatmechIn`](#m-bundlestatmechin) \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `applied_energy_corrections` | array of [`AppliedEnergyCorrectionInBundle`](#m-appliedenergycorrectioninbundle) | no | `[]` |  |  | Applied energy corrections targeting this species's resolved species_entry. Use for scheme-backed corrections such as AEC totals (application_role=aec_total) and BAC totals (application_role=bac_total). ``source_calculation_key`` resolves against the bundle's global calculation namespace; the workflow rejects 422 when the referenced calc is not owned by this species. ``source_conformer_key`` resolves against this species's own ``conformers[*].key`` — a sibling species's conformer is not in scope and is refused. |

- **BundleSpeciesIn.validate_atomless_species_carries_no_structure** (model, after; can refuse via `raise_for_atomless_structure`):

  Refuse a geometry deposited against a participant with no atoms.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008). This model is where a
  declared ``molecule_kind`` and the conformers deposited under it are
  both in hand for the first time, so it is the earliest place the
  contradiction can be named with the key that caused it.

- **BundleSpeciesIn.validate_calc_geometry_keys** (model, after; can refuse): Species '{self.key}' calculation '{calc.key}' (type={calc.type.value}) requires geometry_key.
- **BundleSpeciesIn.validate_calc_conformer_keys** (model, after; can refuse):

  Require a calculation's ``conformer_key`` to name one of this species's conformers.

  Refused here as well as at the workflow seam, and with the same code
  and the same ``context`` (ADR 0017), so a client cannot tell which
  layer caught it. This layer refuses earlier and refuses inside
  ``tckdb-client`` with no server in reach; the seam is the backstop
  for the reach this validator does not have.

  The namespace is this species's own ``conformers[*].key`` and
  nothing else. A sibling species's conformer is not in scope, which
  makes the anchor owner-correct by construction rather than by a
  separate ownership check -- the same property
  ``source_conformer_key`` already relies on.

- **BundleSpeciesIn.validate_calc_geometry_belongs_to_conformer** (model, after; can refuse): Require species-side calculations to reference one of this species's conformers.
- **BundleSpeciesIn.validate_n_imag_matches_species_entry_kind** (model, after; can refuse via `raise_for_blocking_findings`):

  Refuse frequency evidence that contradicts the declared kind.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008). This model is the
  earliest point at which one species entry's declared
  stationary-point kind and that same entry's own frequency
  evidence are both in hand.

| `source_calculations` | array of [`StatmechSourceCalcIn`](#m-statmechsourcecalcin) | no | `[]` |  |  | Statmech → calc links by bundle-local calculation key. Each referenced key must resolve into the bundle's global calc-key namespace and must be owned by this species entry (workflow-layer ownership check). |
| `torsions` | array of [`BundleStatmechTorsionIn`](#m-bundlestatmechtorsionin) | no | `[]` |  |  | Torsional modes. |
| `energy_level_of_theory` | [`LevelOfTheoryRef`](#m-leveloftheoryref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional depositor-declared level of theory the record's energy is claimed to stand at. See ``app.services.calculation_levels`` on the backend for the exact rule; never persisted. |
| `note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional note. |

- **BundleStatmechIn.normalize_point_group** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `point_group`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **BundleStatmechIn.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model, after; can refuse): statmech.source_calculations must be unique by (calculation_key, role).
- **BundleStatmechIn.validate_unique_torsion_indices** (model, after; can refuse): Statmech torsion_index values must be unique within a species.
- **BundleStatmechIn.validate_scientific_interpretation** (model, after; can refuse):

  Scope each requirement to the claim this record actually makes.

  ``statmech_treatment`` is deliberately NOT required. Real producers
  (ARC among them) deposit symmetry, rotational constants and a
  frequency scale factor without naming a treatment; an absent field is
  honest where an invented one would not be.

  Source calculations are likewise not required here. A monatomic
  species has no vibrational modes to point at, and an experimental,
  literature or imported statmech has no calculation at all — forcing
  either to fabricate one buys nothing. Their absence on a *computed*
  record is reported as a structured upload warning at the workflow
  seam, and is enforced as an error only where a rate coefficient
  actually depends on it (the kinetics interpretation seam).

  What IS enforced is the one claim that is self-contradictory when
  unsupported: a rotor-aware treatment is *defined* by the internal
  rotors it treats, so it must list them. With no torsions the correct
  treatment is plain ``rrho``.

- **BundleThermoIn.apply_computed_state_defaults** (model, after):

  Default an omitted ``phase`` to ``gas``, for computed records only.

  Only ``scientific_origin: computed`` gets the default, and only when
  ``phase`` is omitted; an explicit ``null`` is kept as unknown.
  ``reference_pressure_bar`` is never defaulted, for any origin.

- **BundleThermoIn.validate_scientific_content** (model, after; can refuse):

  - Thermo block must include a scalar thermo value, NASA block or thermo points.
  - Thermo points must be unique by temperature_k.

- **BundleThermoIn.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model, after; can refuse):

  One (calculation, role) pair may be claimed once.

  Mirrors ``ThermoInBundle``: the same rule guards the same table
  constraint, and two upload routes disagreeing about it would mean
  one of them turns a nameable 422 into an ``IntegrityError``.

- **BundleThermoIn.normalize_text** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **BundleThermoIn.validate_temperature_range** (model, after; can refuse): tmin_k must be <= tmax_k.

TS-side corrections are never stored as reaction-entry corrections. ``source_calculation_key`` resolves against the bundle's global calculation namespace; the workflow rejects 422 when the referenced calc is not owned by this transition state. ``source_conformer_key`` has nothing to resolve against here — a transition state in this bundle declares no conformers — so setting it is refused rather than ignored. |

Optional but strongly recommended: a deposit without it succeeds and returns a 'transition_state_missing_irc_evidence' upload warning. ``source_calculation_key`` names an irc calculation owned by this transition state. |

- **BundleTransitionStateIn.normalize_text** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `label`, `note`, `unmapped_smiles`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **BundleTransitionStateIn.validate_primary_is_opt** (model, after; can refuse): TS primary calculation must be type 'opt', got '{self.calculation.type.value}'.
- **BundleTransitionStateIn.validate_reaction_coordinate_contract** (model, after; can refuse via `raise_for_blocking_findings`):

  Refuse frequency evidence with no usable reaction coordinate.

  Definitional, therefore blocking (ADR 0008). A transition state
  does not carry a ``stationary_point_kind`` — the entity is the
  claim — so this model is where the declaration and the evidence
  meet. ADR 0012 narrowed what is definitional here: not the
  *count* of imaginary modes, but that there is at least one, that
  exactly one is designated the reaction coordinate, and that no
  undeclared mode is stiff enough to make that designation
  meaningless.

- **BundleTransitionStateIn.validate_evidence_source_is_a_ts_irc_calculation** (model, after; can refuse):

  Evidence must name an ``irc`` calculation owned by this TS.

  Participant/atom completeness needs the bundle's reaction, which this
  nested model cannot see; the enclosing request validates that.

  calculation row is created.

  Enforce constraint_index uniqueness across this calc.

  same ``calculation_constraint`` table at persistence time, so
  ``constraint_index`` must be unique across the union of both lists
  within one calculation.

  DR-0029 Requirement 1: bundle must not carry DB FK ids.

  Walks ``parameters_json`` recursively to catch FK ids that would
  bypass the model's ``extra="forbid"`` (which only enforces
  structural keys, not opaque ``dict`` payloads).

Generic across opt, freq, sp, irc, path_search, scan — input/provenance metadata that does not require a result block. For scan calcs, frozen coordinates may be declared here while the stepped coordinate is declared on scan_result.coordinates. The two lists must not duplicate the same constraint_index. |

- **ComputedReactionCalculationIn.validate_result_matches_type** (model, after; can refuse):

  Mirror ``CalculationWithResultsPayload.validate_result_matches_type``
  for the ``irc_result`` / ``path_search_result`` / ``scan_result``
  fields. The base ``CalculationIn`` has no result-block matrix to
  validate, and the adapter uses ``model_copy(update=...)`` which
  bypasses pydantic validators — so this is the only place where
  mismatched ``(type, irc_result|path_search_result|scan_result)``
  pairs reject as 422 before hitting the persistence seam.

  ``scan_result`` is bundle-only and persisted by the workflow via
  ``persist_calculation_scan`` after the calculation row is created;
  the primitive payload does not carry it.

- **ComputedReactionCalculationIn.validate_constraint_indices_union_unique** (model, after; can refuse):

  Enforce constraint_index uniqueness across the union of
  top-level ``constraints`` and ``scan_result.constraints``.

  Both lists land in the same ``calculation_constraint`` table and
  share the ``(calculation_id, constraint_index)`` composite PK,
  so a duplicate would otherwise surface as an opaque DB error at
  flush time.

<a id="m-conformerin-network-pdep-upload"></a>

### `ConformerIn (network_pdep_upload)`

`app.schemas.workflows.network_pdep_upload`.

- **ConformerUploadStatmechPayload.normalize_optional_text_fields** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `point_group`, `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **ConformerUploadStatmechPayload.validate_electronic_levels** (model, after; can refuse): electronic_levels level_index values must be unique.
- **ConformerUploadStatmechPayload.validate_unique_source_calculation_pairs** (model, after; can refuse):

  Reject duplicate links the way the sibling paths already do.

  ``statmech_source_calculation`` is keyed on
  ``(statmech_id, calculation_id, role)``, so a repeated pair was a
  primary-key violation surfacing as a 500. The bundle and
  standalone statmech uploads validate this; the conformer path
  did not.

  The tuple carries a second discriminator alongside the key, read
  reflectively because this class is also the payload the *backend*
  hands the statmech resolution service — and the standalone
  statmech upload's entries are a subclass that may name a
  calculation by ``existing_calculation_id`` instead of by key.
  Without it, every such entry collapses to ``(None, role)`` and two
  genuinely different calculations sharing a role — one rotor scan
  per torsion, all of them ``role='scan'`` — are refused as a
  duplicate. Nothing changes for a payload built from this package:
  ``StatmechSourceCalcIn`` has no such attribute, so the second
  element is always ``None`` and the rule is the pair it always was.

- **ConformerUploadStatmechPayload.validate_unique_torsion_indices** (model, after; can refuse): One rotor per index, as the sibling upload paths already require.
- **ConformerUploadStatmechPayload.validate_scientific_interpretation** (model, after; can refuse):

  Scope each requirement to the claim this record actually makes.

  ``statmech_treatment`` is deliberately NOT required. Real producers
  (ARC among them) deposit symmetry, rotational constants and a
  frequency scale factor without naming a treatment; an absent field is
  honest where an invented one would not be.

  Source calculations are likewise not required here. A monatomic
  species has no vibrational modes to point at, and an experimental,
  literature or imported statmech has no calculation at all — forcing
  either to fabricate one buys nothing. Their absence on a *computed*
  record is reported as a structured upload warning at the workflow
  seam, and is enforced as an error only where a rate coefficient
  actually depends on it (the kinetics interpretation seam).

  What IS enforced is the one claim that is self-contradictory when
  unsupported: a rotor-aware treatment is *defined* by the internal
  rotors it treats, so it must list them. With no torsions the correct
  treatment is plain ``rrho``.

<a id="m-freqresultpayload"></a>

### `FreqResultPayload`

`tckdb_schemas.fragments.calculation`.

Optional inline result for a frequency calculation.

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Unit | Values / constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n_imag` | integer \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Number of imaginary frequencies. |
| `imag_freq_cm1` | number \| null | no | `null` | cm^-1 |  | Value of the imaginary frequency in cm⁻¹. |
| `zpe_hartree` | number \| null | no | `null` | hartree |  | Zero-point energy in hartree. |
| `modes` | array of [`FrequencyModePayload`](#m-frequencymodepayload) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional per-mode frequency rows. When supplied, ``mode_index`` values must be unique within the payload, and the count of imaginary modes must agree with ``n_imag`` if both are present. |
| `reaction_coordinate_mode_index` | integer \| null | no | `null` |  | >= 1 | ``mode_index`` of the mode the depositor designates the reaction coordinate. ADR 0012 makes this the contract that replaces the old ``n_imag == 1`` gate: a transition state with more than one imaginary mode is accepted only if it says which one is the barrier and is removed from the partition function. Meaningless on a minimum, and refused there. |

- **FreqResultPayload.validate_modes_consistency** (model, after; can refuse):

  - mode_index values must be unique within a freq result. Index {', '.join((str(i) for i in duplicates))} appears more than once, so the list does not say which row is which mode and a consumer reading it cannot reconstruct the spectrum ({W_FREQ_MODE_INDEX_NOT_UNIQUE}). Renumber the modes to the ESS's own 1-based ordering.
  - n_imag={self.n_imag} does not match imaginary mode count {imaginary_count} in modes. The scalar the ESS printed and the frequency list deposited beside it are the same claim made twice, and a record that makes it two ways tells a consumer reading the summary something different from one reading the evidence ({W_FREQ_N_IMAG_DISAGREES_WITH_MODES}). Deposit the complete signed frequency list, or omit modes entirely -- absence is incompleteness, which is accepted, and only contradiction is refused.

- **FreqResultPayload.validate_reaction_coordinate_designation** (model, after; can refuse):

  The designated reaction coordinate must be an imaginary mode.

  Checked here rather than in
  :func:`~tckdb_schemas.stationary_point.evaluate_transition_state_frequency`
  because it is a statement about the payload's internal
  consistency, not about the chemistry: an index naming a real mode
  or naming nothing at all is a malformed record whatever kind of
  stationary point it describes.

A harmonic frequency scale factor is fit against a program's own build-level vibrational frequencies, which change between releases of the same program (correction-scheme-provenance plan v2 §6, mirroring ``EnergyCorrectionSchemeRef.software``'s reasoning) -- so the factor is release-specific, not merely program-specific. Only ``name`` is required; a depositor who knows only the program resolves to the version-less release row for it. Null means software-agnostic or unknown. |
| `source_literature` | [`LiteratureUploadRequest`](#m-literatureuploadrequest) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Structured literature provenance, when available. Mutually informative with ``workflow_tool_release``; either, both, or neither may be supplied. |
| `workflow_tool_release` | [`WorkflowToolReleaseRef`](#m-workflowtoolreleaseref) \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Workflow tool (e.g. ARC) whose data file was the proximate source, when the factor was looked up from a tool table rather than directly from a paper. |
| `note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional descriptive note. Never used for dedupe. |

- **FreqScaleFactorRef.normalize_text** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.

<a id="m-frequencymodepayload"></a>

### `FrequencyModePayload`

`tckdb_schemas.fragments.calculation`.

One vibrational mode within a frequency calculation result.

Unknown keys are silently ignored.

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Unit | Values / constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode_index` | integer | yes |  |  | >= 1 | 1-based ordering from the ESS output. |
| `frequency_cm1` | number | yes |  | cm^-1 |  | Harmonic frequency in cm⁻¹; negative for imaginary modes. |
| `is_imaginary` | boolean | yes |  |  |  | Whether the mode is imaginary. Required and consistent with the sign of ``frequency_cm1``. |
| `reduced_mass_amu` | number \| null | no | `null` | amu | > 0 | Reduced mass in amu, when reported. |
| `force_constant_mdyne_angstrom` | number \| null | no | `null` | mdyn/angstrom |  | Force constant in mDyne/Ångström, when reported. |
| `ir_intensity_km_mol` | number \| null | no | `null` | km/mol | >= 0 | IR intensity in km/mol, when reported. |
| `raman_activity` | number \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Raman activity (Å⁴/amu), when reported. |
| `symmetry_label` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Irreducible representation label (e.g. ``"A1"``, ``"E"``), when reported. |
| `imaginary_disposition` | `ImaginaryModeDisposition` \| null | no | `null` |  | `rigid_body_residue`, `torsion`, `ring_pucker`, `intermolecular`, `symmetry_breaking`, `unassigned` | What this imaginary mode *is*, when it is not the reaction coordinate. Declared by the depositor, never inferred — TCKDB stores no normal-mode displacement vectors to infer it from. Only meaningful on an imaginary mode; setting it on a real one is refused rather than ignored. See ADR 0012. |
| `note` | string \| null | no | `null` |  |  | Optional free-text annotation. |

- **FrequencyModePayload.validate_sign_matches_is_imaginary** (model, after; can refuse):

  - is_imaginary=True requires frequency_cm1 < 0. Negate the magnitude at the producer boundary before upload.
  - frequency_cm1 < 0 requires is_imaginary=True.
  - imaginary_disposition={self.imaginary_disposition.value} was set on mode {self.mode_index}, which is not imaginary. A disposition says what an imaginary mode is instead of the reaction coordinate; on a real mode it has no meaning.

- **KineticsTunnelingApplicationUpload.validate_model_inputs** (model, after; can refuse):

  - result artifact requires both calculation ref and SHA-256.
  - tunneling_application.model must be a correction model, not 'none'.
  - SCT path artifact requires both calculation ref and SHA-256.
  - frequency_sign_convention must be 'negative_imaginary_cm1'.
  - Wigner/Eckart tunneling requires imaginary_frequency_cm1.
  - imaginary_frequency_cm1 must be negative under negative_imaginary_cm1.
  - Eckart tunneling requires reactant/product energies, forward/reverse barriers, and energy conventions.
  - SCT tunneling requires a path-integral artifact.
  - convention_note is required when an energy convention is 'other'.
  - tunneling_application.model='other' requires model_identifier, a machine token naming the correction actually applied (e.g. 'zero_curvature_tunneling').
  - tunneling_application.model='other' requires a result artifact (calculation ref + SHA-256) so the correction stays replayable.
  - model_identifier is only valid when model='other'; the named models are already identified by 'model'.

| `a` | number | yes |  |  |  |  |
| `a_units` | `ArrheniusAUnits` \| null | no | `null` |  | `per_s`, `cm3_mol_s`, `cm3_molecule_s`, `m3_mol_s`, `cm6_mol2_s`, `cm6_molecule2_s`, `m6_mol2_s` |  |
| `n` | number \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `reported_ea` | number \| null | no | `null` |  |  |  |
| `reported_ea_units` | `ActivationEnergyUnits` \| null | no | `null` |  | `j_mol`, `kj_mol`, `cal_mol`, `kcal_mol` |  |

<a id="m-networkchannelin"></a>

### `NetworkChannelIn`

`app.schemas.workflows.network_pdep_upload`.

A directed phenomenological channel between two network states.

Unknown keys are refused.

| Field | Type | Req | Default | Unit | Values / constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |  |  | length >= 1 |  |
| `source_state_key` | string | yes |  |  | length >= 1 | Local key of the source state. |
| `sink_state_key` | string | yes |  |  | length >= 1 | Local key of the sink state. |
| `kind` | `NetworkChannelKind` | yes |  |  | `isomerization`, `association`, `dissociation`, `stabilization`, `exchange` | Macroscopic channel classification (association, ...). |
| `mechanism` | `NetworkChannelMechanism` | no | `"elementary"` |  | `elementary`, `well_skipping` | Mechanistic attribution. Defaults to ``elementary``, so an existing payload that names its ``microreaction_paths`` is unaffected. |
| `microreaction_paths` | array of `NetworkChannelMicroReactionIn` | no | `[]` |  |  | The elementary step(s) this channel is attributed to. |

- **NetworkChannelIn.validate_source_ne_sink** (model, after; can refuse): source_state_key and sink_state_key must differ.
- **NetworkChannelIn.validate_paths_match_mechanism** (model, after; can refuse):

  Path cardinality is fixed by the declared mechanism, never optional.

  This is what keeps the relaxation additive and non-silent: a channel
  that supplies no paths is only ever accepted when it has *said* it is
  well-skipping.

| `pressure_units` | `PressureUnit` \| null | no | `null` |  | `bar`, `atm` | Units the fit's pressure axis is expressed in. |

- **NetworkKineticsIn.normalize_text** (model, after): applies `normalize_optional_text` to `note`: Trim optional text inputs and collapse blank strings to None.
- **NetworkKineticsIn.validate_source_ne_sink** (model, after; can refuse):

  - channel_key is required (or both legacy source_state_key and sink_state_key).
  - legacy source_state_key and sink_state_key must be supplied together.
  - source_state_key and sink_state_key must differ.

- **NetworkKineticsIn.validate_model_payload** (model, after; can refuse):

  Chebyshev and PLOG are supported; tabulated is not yet.

  Exactly one model sub-block must be present, matching ``model_kind``.
  The tabulated (``network_kinetics_point``) write path is still
  unimplemented; reject it explicitly.

- **NetworkKineticsIn.validate_ranges** (model, after; can refuse):

  - tmin_k must be less than or equal to tmax_k.
  - pmin_bar must be less than or equal to pmax_bar.
